title: Horrible
content:
I’m extremely dissatisfied with my experience using Shopify and regret signing up.

Payout expectations were not made clear up front. I discovered after setup that even though my payout schedule was set to daily, that did not mean I would receive my funds the next business day. As a new account, each daily payout was effectively delayed by about 7 business days, which was completely different from what I expected and completely different from my previous payment processor, where I received funds the next business day from the start. The wording around daily payouts was misleading in practice because it suggested faster access to funds than what actually happened. That distinction between payout schedule and actual settlement timing was not made obvious during onboarding, and it should have been spelled out much more clearly before I committed to the platform.

The setup experience for the online store was also confusing and frustrating. Instead of one clear, cohesive onboarding flow, the process felt fragmented and difficult to follow. Basic setup did not feel intuitive, and it often seemed like important information was split across different areas rather than presented in one place. The platform did not feel user friendly, especially for someone trying to get a store operational efficiently.

The hardware setup was another major source of frustration. It took several days to figure out how to get everything working because the instructions for the overall system were not cohesive. Rather than having one clear end-to-end setup path, I had to piece together information from separate places, which made the process far more difficult and time-consuming than it should have been.

The overall experience has fallen far short of what was promised. Between the payout timing surprise, the lack of clear up-front communication, the confusing online store setup, and the difficult hardware setup, Shopify has been extremely disappointing and troublesome to use. At multiple points, it felt more like I was fighting the system than being supported by it.

Even the feedback process has been confusing. I was given a link to submit feedback, but it opened what appeared to be a chat and did not clearly indicate whether my feedback was actually being formally submitted. I couldn’t even get an email or form to send feedback so I had to resort to leaving a review. That added even more frustration to an already disappointing experience.

Avoid using this app before it’s too late. I’ve wasted tons of money and worse - time - on this terrible system.

title: Lots of room for improvement
content:
There are a lot of things that I like about the Shopify ap-
But there are more that I dislike about the whole program in general:
First off, with the amount of fraudulent orders that I receive, I lose money every transaction. The money is taken and then the order is canceled by a FLOW and then the money is returned but I lose money because of two reasons: a line of credit that’s in repayment, and the fee that Shopify takes even though I made zero profit from the refunded order. It’s absolute BS.
Second: it takes days to put money INTO the main balance account. So if you’re like me and don’t trust money to be left in anything but a central banking account, and this overdraft of fees happens after a fraudulent order, you get a million emails and notifications and threats while still waiting for funds to process that were initiated multiple days ago.
Third: it’s not an instant pay system like square, which means I operate on a separate system for markets, to instantly have the money in my account and not wait for a payout,  because the level of customization Shopify offers for branding is the best part about it.

title: BEWARE - Terrible AI customer service.
content:
I’ve been using Shopify professionally and personally for over a decade. Unfortunately, like many tech companies they have switched their customer service experience to AI chatbots. It’s incredibly difficult to reach a human being for help. And when you finally do, it’s takes days of waiting to get resolutions. They no longer prioritize their customers concerns.

Shopify’s own Bill Pay feature that they offer for their Shopify Balance accounts did not pay my studio rent on time 2 months in a row despite being assured my rent payment would process. The first month they did offer a $50 reimbursement for the inconvenience. The second month this happened (which in my mind is worse because I had already spent hours upon hours dealing with them and their bill pay processing company Melio the first time to get it resolved) They refused to offer me a credit or even a written letter explaining their own  failure in paying bills with the money that was in my shopify balance account.

If you are a small business  just starting out save yourself the hassle and try Square. I have friends that swear by it. I am so disappointed with Shopify that I’m considering building a whole new Wordpress website just to get as far away from them as I can.

title: Shopify app update
content:
Hi Shopify team,

The recent update to the Shopify mobile app has made it much harder to manage inventory.

Previously, I could open a collection and quickly see the stock levels for every product within it. As a bakery owner, I use collections to plan production, and this view was one of the features I relied on most every week.

Now I have to open products individually or navigate through several extra screens, which adds a lot of unnecessary time to a task I perform daily.

Please consider bringing back the ability to view inventory quantities directly within collections on the mobile app, or add it as an optional list view. It was a simple but incredibly valuable feature for merchants managing stock.

Thank you for considering this feedback.

title: UPDATES ARE TRASH
content:
The “Spring26” Updates (released in June26) only reenforce how little Shopify understands about how this app is used. Reducing the font and minimizing the screen space for the BASE metrics is inane. Prioritizing secondary metrics like Payouts over Total Sales is illogical, nor do most users of this app need / should have access to this information. Monopolizing the screen display with oversized banners heralding the addition of new functionality - often paid - feels like the app is being taken over by adds.
On an accessibility level - the “casino” style motion used to display Total Sales, combined with the reduced font size and screen placement, makes the most important and most commonly used metric on this screen prohibitively hard to read.
Your AI-driven design has taken over and it seems that you now neglect consulting or beta testing with your actual accounts, forcing us to waste our time in Support requesting the removed functionality back. As a result, Shopify is becoming unusable. Every update makes it worse and completely degrades and destroys workflow. DO BETTER SHOPIFY.

title: Best E-commerce platform ever!
content:
There’s a reason Shopify continues to dominate the conversation around modern commerce. Most platforms give you tools. Shopify gives you infrastructure the kind that quietly removes friction so brands can focus on building culture instead of battling software.

What stands out isn’t just the ecosystem or scalability. It’s the philosophy behind it. Shopify understands that great commerce today is equal parts technology, storytelling, and customer experience. The platform feels engineered by people who actually understand entrepreneurs.

From independent startups to established brands doing serious volume, Shopify somehow manages to stay powerful without becoming unnecessarily complicated. That balance is rare.

In an era where most tech companies overpromise and underdeliver, Shopify has consistently done the opposite. Clean execution, constant innovation, and a platform that genuinely helps brands grow instead of trapping them in complexity.

That’s not hype. That’s just good infrastructure.

content: About a month ago, Shopify updated the way photos are uploaded into a listing.  Since that time, we’ve had to jump through two hoops to add photos.  First, we have to add the photos to our Shopify account.  Then, we have to upload them into the listing.  The photos ALWAYS upload in reverse order to what is selected.  It’s necessary to try to move them back in the intended order, and half the time, the app won’t allow you to do that.  And even when you get them in the correct intended order, when the listing saves, it reverts the photos.  This update or “enhancement” is insane, and not in a good way.  I am going to be cancelling my Shopify account due to this issue, as well as the price increase we suffered last year.  It’s just not worth it when I can do all of my business, and create a website through Etsy, for a small fraction of the cost and hassle.

title: Issue going
content:
I’ve encountered several frustrating issues while using the Shopify app that have impacted my workflow:

Order Fulfillment Glitch: When fulfilling orders and scanning the tracking number, the app redirects me to the home page instead of confirming the tracking. I then have to go back to the orders page and manually confirm the order again, which is a repetitive and time-consuming process.
Website Customization Problems: While customizing my store, especially when sorting fields or blocks, the app freezes on the website and I have to refresh the page repeatedly. This issue happens consistently, which slows down my customization process and affects overall productivity.
Order Management Issue: When I try to open the orders section, the app now unexpectedly displays a message saying “Manage your orders – you will be notified when you get your first order.” The same message appears when accessing abandoned carts as well, which is confusing and prevents me from accessing important order and cart details.
These issues have made managing my store more difficult, and I hope they get addressed in future updates.

title: 1 month of silence from Shopify and $1,090 has disappeared from my payout account.
content:
I have so far had an absolutely terrible experience, and it is culminating in what seems to be $1,090 stolen from my payout account (and not in Balance either), with no help in sight.

I have messaged support about this 7-8 times over the course of the month and never get an answer. And I pay for a lower tier of Shopify, so I am not entitled to phone support. At this point I believe Shopify has taken my money. I have still NEVER received an email about this (in my spam folder or otherwise.) Terrible customer service and terrible resolution team.

title: Account Recovery Process Stressful
content: Recently I had to get a new phone number, I was able to sign in on my computer but forgot to update the number on my Shopify account. Then to my already stressful life my computer’s hard drive crashed. I was unable to recovery my recovery codes or sign into my Shopify account from my new computer or phone. I contacted Shopify support, which in itself was even more stressful because to reach someone you had to select your store to sign in and I could not. After a few hours, I was finally able to reach someone by chat. I was informed that they would be submitting an account recovery request but there was no timeline on resolution. Two weeks later I got an email to submit documentation to validate that I am the owner. I submitted the documents and hoped that over the next 48-72 hours I would hear something. It has now been another week with no further responses. I am unable to access orders to fulfill, resulting in a loss in revenue which I informed the agent this fact when requesting account recovery. There simply should be a much better process for account recovery with such a large corporation, and business owner’s entire business livelihood attached to the platform. I’m likely going to have to refund any and all sales and possibly have to send out some sort of discount and apology to ensure I retain customers. I am still being charged the fees for a service I can’t use and losing money. I’ve been with Shopify since 2018 and I never considered this process would be so complicated and lengthy. I am now likely going to seek another more reliable platform that considers the urgency for these sort of issues. I suggest saving your recovery codes offline, print them, or save to a cloud platform that you can always access. Luckily I have Etsy and have been able to redirect some customers to this option to shop our products.

author: Reeferss

title: Shopify is great however
content:
Shopify is great. It’s a one stop shop with tons of third party apps that work with it as you grow or to help fit your site to your business. But with every great thing there is always some downfalls.

My biggest issue is Shopify locks you into their payment provider or merchant. Shopify payments is ran by stripe, they will not negotiate rates and will charge a percentage fee if you do not use shop pay as your main merchant. This could affect some businesses, depending on what type of business you are, or what you sell.

My next issue has to do with third party apps, as they don’t always sync 100% of the time. This can cause order issues and intern loose customers. As well as the more apps you add the slower your site becomes. This also goes for if you want to ever develop an app.

My last biggest issue is the reliability. as by using Shopify, you are relying that Shopify will keep your store up and live at all times. However Shopify is not perfect and I would say at least once a month if not more we experience some glitch or downtime on the site.

Conclusion,
Shopify is great with some kinks that still need to be worked out. Intern it’s probably one of the easiest website / e-commerce building tool out there with compatibility to almost any style of business. However, like any big corporation, they try to lock you in and this can course some issues as you grow:)

title: Beware- Shopify a No show for extremely urgent situation
content:
I launched a book sale using Shopify yesterday. After 2k sales in 24 hours, I can say I’m overjoyed with the first day of sales. Unfortunately I have received dozens of messages, emails, dm’s from potential customers saying they are unable to access the website to purchase books. These of course, are only the customers who have taken the time to reach out.
This started at the beginning of sales yesterday and has continued today. My developer was on the phone with Shopify yesterday, I sent emails, and also was on the phone beginning again early this morning. After all of these calls we were given directives  to ask our customers to take their phones off of Wi-Fi to place orders, or try putting items in the cart and then choosing the payment method. Or use another device to access the site or change browsers when they were told the site was unsafe. We purchased a separate domain through Shopify as they suggested to funnel all of our transactions, and the website is being flagged as unsafe.
Shopify will not resolve the problem or put anyone on their technical team to immediately take care of this issue. I was told the tech team does not do phone calls, only emails. Also, they are backed up today.
I have stopped sharing about the book launch because we are experiencing so many customer problems regarding accessing the site and checking out.  Very disappointed that a brand with so many resources is unwilling to step up and resolve this for a small business owner.

title: Expensive to keep traffic coming
content:
Bad points I’ll start with.
If you want site visitors you need to have a good amount of money to get them to your store via social media and google ads. If you spend around £2000 that will get you around 30k shop visitors (obviously depending on what you’re selling) this may sound like a lot of store visitors but because your a ‘new’ website not many will actually buy. You are kind of forced to add apps to help you sell, all these apps have massive up selling techniques by offering you a free trial, then start a monthly charge there after so watch out for these.

Good points.
Shopify response time to questions are unbelievably fast, they are willing to help at every stage and have a fantastic customer service (I’m really impressed)

Shopify is user friendly and even getting down to do abit of coding isn’t difficult with their walkthrough guides.

So to conclude shopify is great to use, very user friendly, customer service is great but if you’re drop shipping or you have a product to sell with no current social media followers you’ll have to dig deep in your pockets to keep the traffic coming. Maybe you might have a winning product and you’ll make a load of money or you’ll be like the majority and spend money on ads and reap no rewards short term (I’ve only been going 6 weeks so I can’t comment on long term, I will update this review once I’ve got another 5 months under my belt and another couple of grand spent on ads)

title: Recent updates made photo upload a nightmare
content:
I run my business on my iPhone. This app is useable but there are several areas needing improvement.

To change inventory, sku or the barcode on a variant, you have to go through multiple screens. There is no way to bulk edit on this app. No way to reorder variants. Editing these product fields on the app is a slow process and unnecessarily so.

The recent version made photo uploads an arduous process. First you have the pre-select photos from your camera roll. Then (if you are lucky and the app didn’t freeze), you have to re-select the photos from the pre-selected group before you can upload to your item. And then the updated photos do not refresh unless I close and reopen the app. Are you kidding me?

Shopify development team, here are some constructive suggestions to improve this app:

— add bulk edit function

— display variant name, price, inventory quantity, sku, barcode on the SAME screen to allow for quicker editing (instead of nesting these items within multiple screens)

— make photo uploads a 1 step process instead of a 2 step process

It’s obviously a sneaky ploy to make it easier for people to get started, but if you’re a bit of a procrastinator like me, you could easily find your money on hold while you argue with Shopify. Annoyingly, they have no awareness at all of U.K. law and things like the data protection act and will ask you for your suppliers’ or customers’ information regardless. Do the right thing Shopify and get all this done upfront before sellers get all busy.

title: It’s not the app, it’s Shopify.
content:
Use this service at your own risk. I’ve been running a website through Shopify for over a year now, and out of nowhere they froze my money and are refusing to give it back. It’s been a month to the day, they owe me over $3,000, and there’s no sign of the money being moved despite the fact that they said they removed any and all holds from my account days ago.

Additionally, new users should be very aware of what they’re selling through Shopify. It’s incredibly easy to accidentally stock an item that doesn’t seem like it could possibly be legally copyrighted, and then have Shopify break your door down for it. They do not like to tell you their rules outright, they like to let you drown a bit before telling you that if you mess up again they’ll shove your head back underwater.

Additionally, it would appear that the majority of the recent reviews left on here were left by their admins in an attempt to make themselves look better. A bunch of the reviews are almost identical, apart from the fact that they all have crazy names.

title: Data won’t refresh
content:
There’s a little t to like about this app but it’s all overshadowed for me by the fact that it’s near impossible to get it to display up-to-the minute information. Isn’t the whole point of having an app like this on your phone so that you can get a quick snapshot of where things stand at the moment?

And then randomly - maybe after you’ve been looking at the screen for 6 minutes- boom, you current information just pops in there unceremoniously.

It’s a weird miss for an app that otherwise was clearly very thoughtfully developed.

title: PLEASE FIX THIS ONE THING
content:
When adding a product to my store, I am unable to select multiple photos to add to the product at a time.

To those people who regularly add new products and like to include many different photos to show all the different product options like colours and styles: be warned, you will spend more of your time in this app manually selecting and adding one photo at a time to one product at a time than anything else.

To those whose selection rarely changes: you’ll still spend more of your time adding photos in this tedious manor than anything else you do during your initial set up.
